topology_reasoning.what_is_this_device: A symmetric directional coupler: two identical single-mode waveguides enter at opposite corners (top-left/bottom-left), are brought close together by mirrored smooth S-bends into a short central parallel section separated by a sub-half-micron gap, then separate again by mirrored S-bends to the output ports. The image shows exactly two constant-width strips, mirror-symmetric about the horizontal midline and left-right symmetric about the vertical midline; no tapers, no third feature.
topology_reasoning.how_it_works: In the central section the two guides are close enough (gap ~0.29 um << wavelength) that their modal evanescent fields overlap, splitting the system into even/odd supermodes with different propagation constants. Light launched in one guide beats between the guides with transfer length L_pi = pi/(beta_even - beta_odd); the power splitting ratio is set by the effective interaction length (central parallel section plus the adiabatic contribution of the S-bend approach regions) relative to L_pi, and by the gap, which sets the supermode splitting exponentially. The S-bends bring the guides together gradually to avoid junction scattering; the port separation at the ends decouples the guides.
function_defining_knobs: coupling_gap: edge-to-edge separation in the central section - exponentially controls the even/odd supermode splitting, hence the coupling strength per unit length
coupling_length: length of the central parallel section - the primary transfer-length knob that dials the splitting ratio
wg_width: guide width - sets modal confinement (and with the gap, the supermode splitting)
io_separation: port center-to-center separation - sets decoupling at the ports within the fixed 3 um footprint
sbend_length: horizontal extent of each cosine S-bend - controls bend adiabaticity and the parasitic coupling accumulated during approach

measurements_from_target.method: column-wise black-run analysis of component.png under the calibration (88 px/um in x, 149 px/um in y, ink bbox y 113..560)
measurements_from_target.notes: Width is constant along the guides (0.658-0.691 um across columns; excess on slopes is the vertical-cut widening of a slanted strip). Total ink pixels 316396 are fully explained by the two strips - no third feature, no border bar.

parametric_model.centerline: per arm: straight lead (straight_in) at +/- io_separation/2, cosine S-bend of horizontal extent sbend_length down to +/- (coupling_gap+wg_width)/2, straight coupling_length, mirrored cosine S-bend back, straight lead; sampled centerline -> gf.Path -> extrude at wg_width on layer (1,0)
parametric_model.shape_choice: raised-cosine S-bend fits the measured centerline within ~0.05 um at every probed column; the measured 1.6 um gap plateau plus the cosine's flat tails reproduces the observed 8.2-9.8 um plateau

lengths_json_semantics: lengths.json is computed from the built paths every run, never hand-entered, and follows the two-arm contract homi.spec_optimization validates (delta_length_um == |top - bottom|, which is structurally 0 for this symmetric coupler). The coupler's own function-knob readback is coupling_section_measured_um: the geometry-measured length of the central minimum-separation section. An earlier draft put that span in delta_length_um; _validate_arms correctly rejected it and it was moved to its own field.

iterations.change_made: Initial build: cosine S-bends, wg_width 0.666 (0.665 rejected by the 2-dbu grid), gap 0.29, straight_in 0.9, sbend_length 7.25. Postmortem from diff: total length summed to 17.9 not 18.0 (arithmetic slip -> blue bar at right edge), S-bend shape systematically off (red outer / blue inner lobes: target descends faster early), ink height 3.006 vs 3.000 (outer fringes).

Least-squares fit of a skewed-cosine family (t^p warp) to the measured centerline: straight_in 1.478, sbend_length 6.728, skew 0.781, coupling_length 1.588 (18.000 closure), io_separation 2.334 (ink height exactly 3.0), gap 0.287; out-bend warp time-mirrored so the right half is the exact x-mirror. Residual: strips render ~2.3 px fatter than target; +/-2-3 px systematic wiggle along bends (family misfit, rms 7.7 nm).

Replaced the cosine family with the fitted two-arc S-bend (arc-line-arc fit collapsed the line to zero): bend_radius_in 15.781 (port side), bend_radius_out 25.959 (coupling side), angle derived from the radii and the lateral offset; centerline rms fell 7.7 -> 3.3 nm. Width cut 0.666 -> 0.650 with io_separation 2.350 keeping outer edges pinned at +/-1.5. Overcorrected: precision 0.998 / recall 0.982 -> now ~1.5-2 px net thin, worst on bends where the target widens beyond slope-projection.

Width 0.650 -> 0.656, io_separation 2.344, gap 0.296 (min center separation held at 0.952), coupling_length 1.090 re-closing 18.000 with straight_in 0.865. Remaining FN concentrated on the bends: target strips reach 102-103 px vertical there vs ~100 for constant-width extrusion - the source rendering fattens strokes with slope.

Slope-tracking width: each arc segment extruded with a linear taper from wg_width at its flat-tangent end to sbend_mid_width 0.670 at the max-slope R_in/R_out joint (gf.path.transition + extrude_transition; leads and coupling section stay at wg_width so the gap is unaffected). Segments constructed analytically (exact circles, mirrored right half) after index-slicing the composed path proved fragile. Residual is +/-1 px antialiasing noise uniformly distributed (FP 1838 / FN 1175 px, edges within 1 px everywhere); stopped here as the honest best - a 6th iteration would chase sub-pixel noise.

final.primitives_used: gf.path.straight + gf.path.arc composition (analytic centerlines), gf.path.extrude, gf.path.transition/extrude_transition (taper), @gf.cell assembly; no gf.components stencils, no raw polygons

knob_verification.verify_knob_response_as_briefed: delta_length_ok false (structural: symmetric arms make delta_length_um identically 0 - the MZI-shaped check cannot respond for this device class); area grew 6.56 um2 = exactly 2x the single-guide expectation because the knob extends BOTH guides
knob_verification.verify_knob_response_two_arm_coefficient: with width_um = 2*wg_width = 1.312 the tool's gdstk area check passes (6.56 um2 growth, 0% error)
knob_verification.direct_span_probe: coupling_section_measured_um 1.399 -> 6.399 (+5.000 for +5.0 knob), device_length +5.0, min_center_separation unchanged
